# 17 — Documentation website experience

## A product surface, not an autogenerated dumping ground

Documentation must demonstrate the same clarity and responsiveness we promise. Keep an existing healthy docs stack. If no site exists, use a static-first system such as Astro/Starlight with isolated React examples; Starlight supplies documentation-oriented navigation/search/theme infrastructure. This choice is an implementation proposal, not permission to rebuild an existing site unnecessarily. [R18]

## Information architecture

Start → Installation → First component → Add semantics → Compose workspace → Connect agent. Then Components, Visuals, Workspace, Data & contracts, Integrations, Recipes, Customization, Accessibility/performance, API/migrations, and OSS/Pro. Users can enter at any level without reading an architecture dissertation.

Every component page has name, one-sentence task, stability/license badge, when to use/avoid, live preview, minimal code, relevant configuration, data requirements, controlled/adaptive behavior, interactions, accessibility, performance limits, API, and related recipes. Default open view prioritizes the component; schema/inspector details are secondary tabs/disclosures, not a wall of controls.

## Layout specification

Desktop: top brand/navigation/search/theme, restrained left navigation, main reading column around 68–76 characters, optional right local table of contents. Expanded playground can occupy the content region without squeezing into article width. At narrow widths, navigation becomes an accessible drawer; on-page TOC collapses; examples remain usable and code overflow is local. Mobile hero doesn't consume the entire first screen.

Use one clear active item, breadcrumb only when useful, stable anchors and version-aware search. Keep experimental/Pro state explicit before users invest effort. Do not hide “how do I actually use this?” behind marketing cards.

## Interactive examples

Preview/Code tabs plus optional Inspect, not five equally dominant panes. Controls expose useful task variants: width, density, locale, data state, explicit/adaptive mode. Reset restores a deterministic seed. Users can select/filter and see linked updates immediately. Test fixture is synthetic with visible labeling; no fake current benchmark/price claims.

A “Try agent” area must state whether it runs an actual connected model or replays a deterministic example. Never fake a working MCP connection with a timed animation. For real mode show target workspace, connection/permission status, cancel, and operation outcome. Private keys are entered only through an approved backend/session flow, not stored in the playground browser.

Heavy examples hydrate on visibility or user activation. Static API content renders without JavaScript. Don't mount every interactive catalog example at once. Sandbox/editor dependencies are isolated from ordinary docs navigation. Error boundary and reset recover failed examples without blanking the page.

## Public page requirements

Installation commands are generated from actual package names/version and tested consumer fixtures. No fictitious `npm install` instruction. Copy buttons have feedback and keyboard focus. API tables derive from canonical contracts/types; handwritten pages explain meaning/tradeoffs. Search indexes correct versions and includes synonyms such as currency/money, brush/range filter, adaptive/responsive.

Machine-readable docs/Markdown index can improve discovery but do not promise all agents will read it. Keep canonical links, deprecation banners, migration guides and runnable source references. Test broken links and code examples in CI.

## Visual direction

Use the same tokens as components with a documentation-specific readable typography scale. Refined neutral surfaces, one accent, strong hierarchy, restrained motion. No content-overlapping sticky regions, excessive glass effects, decorative code wallpaper, or misleading badges such as “production-ready” without release evidence.

## Usability acceptance

A new user finds standalone Table usage, currency conversion rules, linked filters and MCP setup through navigation/search. They can distinguish OSS versus Pro and stable versus experimental in one page. They complete the first component and one semantic comparison from docs without private assistance. Review at 360/768/1280/1600 CSS-pixel viewport widths plus component-container resizing; these are test fixtures, not device-support guarantees.

`docs-site/` includes authored page blueprints and sample public copy to seed the site. It does not replace running the actual component examples from the PoC.
